progressionInfo.name: Circle of Fifths: Advanced Harmonic Movement
progressionInfo.subtitle: Explore sophisticated progressions that move through keys using the powerful relationships in the circle of fifths. Master advanced harmonic movement and sophisticated voice leading.

chordDiagrams.title: Basic Circle of Fifths (Key of C)
chordDiagrams.description: C - Am - Dm - G: This basic progression demonstrates root movement by descending fifths (or ascending fourths).
practiceNotes: Root movement: C (down 5th to) Am (down 5th to) Dm (down 5th to) G
Notice how each chord shares common tones with the next
This is the foundation for all circle-based progressions

chordDiagrams.title: Extended Circle Progression
chordDiagrams.description: C - Am - Dm - G - Em - Am - Dm - G: Extending the circle creates longer, more sophisticated progressions spanning multiple measures.
practiceNotes: Each chord's root is a perfect fifth below the previous chord's root
The sequence can repeat and extend as long as desired
Notice the pattern: I-vi-ii-V-iii-vi-ii-V

chordDiagrams.title: Jazz Circle with Seventh Chords
chordDiagrams.description: Cmaj7 - Am7 - Dm7 - G7 - Em7 - Am7 - Dm7 - G7: Jazz musicians use seventh chords for richer harmony and smoother voice leading.
practiceNotes: Voice leading: the 7th of each chord resolves down to the 3rd of the next chord
These voicings create much smoother transitions than open chords
Essential vocabulary for jazz guitar playing

advancedApplications.title: Circle Progressions in Different Keys
advancedApplications.description: The 4-chord circle pattern transposed to common guitar-friendly keys.
items: C Major: C - Am - Dm - G
G Major: G - Em - Am - D
D Major: D - Bm - Em - A
A Major: A - F#m - Bm - E
F Major: F - Dm - Gm - C

advancedApplications.title: Tritone Substitutions
advancedApplications.description: Replace dominant chords with chords a tritone away for sophisticated jazz harmony.
items: Instead of: Am7 - D7 - G, try: Am7 - Ab7 - G
The tritone sub shares the same guide tones (3rd and 7th)
Creates chromatic bass motion for smoother voice leading
Common in jazz standards and modern harmony

advancedApplications.title: Chromatic Movement
advancedApplications.description: Add chromatic passing chords between circle changes for smoother voice leading.
items: Basic: C - Am - Dm - G
With passing: C - C#dim7 - Dm - G
The diminished chord acts as a chromatic connector
Creates a sophisticated smooth bass line movement

advancedApplications.title: Voice Leading & Bass Movement
advancedApplications.description: Circle progressions feature a strong descending bass line that reinforces the harmonic movement.
items: Bass pattern descends by fifths: C - A - D - G - E - A - D - G
Common tones connect adjacent chords smoothly
Inner voices move by step while bass moves by fifth
This creates the strongest possible sense of harmonic direction

examples.title: Bach Chorales and Fugues
examples.description: Circle progressions are fundamental to Baroque counterpoint
examples.detail: Bach frequently used circle of fifths sequences as the harmonic backbone of his compositions.

examples.title: Mozart and Beethoven Sonatas
examples.detail: Sequence patterns often move through the circle of fifths in sonata development sections.

examples.title: Sequence Patterns
examples.detail: The circle provides a systematic way to modulate through related keys.

examples.title: Modulation to Related Keys
examples.detail: Adjacent keys on the circle share the most notes, making modulations smooth and natural.

examples.title: "Autumn Leaves"
examples.description: Circle progression in the bridge section
examples.detail: Bridge: Am7 - D7 - G - G / Em7 - A7 - D - D. One of the most famous circle of fifths examples.

examples.title: "All the Things You Are"
examples.detail: The entire harmony is built on extended circle of fifths movement through multiple keys.

examples.title: "Giant Steps"
examples.description: Coltrane changes - circle pushed to extremes
examples.detail: John Coltrane's revolutionary composition takes circle relationships and divides them into major thirds.

examples.title: "Fly Me to the Moon"
examples.detail: The verse follows a clear circle of fifths pattern that gives the song its elegant harmonic motion.

examples.title: "All of Me"
examples.detail: E7 - Am - Am / Dm - G7 - C. Classic example of circle of fifths in a standard.

practiceCategories.title: Progressive Learning
items: Learn the basic pattern: Start with C-Am-Dm-G
Understand the theory: Identify the fifth relationships
Practice in all keys: Start with easier keys (G, D, A)
Add seventh chords: Practice jazz voicings
Work on voice leading: Focus on smooth transitions
Learn real songs: Apply to jazz standards and classical pieces

practiceCategories.title: Technical Exercises
items: Practice circle progressions with a metronome
Work on fingerpicking patterns over the circle
Practice with different rhythmic feels (swing, straight, bossa)
Use alternate chord voicings in different positions
Practice smooth transitions between barre chord shapes

practiceCategories.title: Musical Applications
items: Improvise melodies over circle progressions
Write songs using circle of fifths movement
Analyze famous songs for hidden circle patterns
Practice modulating between keys using the circle
Learn to hear and recognize fifth relationships by ear

notatedExercises.title: Basic Circle of Fifths (C-Am-Dm-G)
notatedExercises.description: The fundamental 4-chord circle pattern demonstrating root movement by descending fifths.
practiceNotes: Root movement: C (down 5th to) Am (down 5th to) Dm (down 5th to) G
Listen for the common tones between adjacent chords
This is the building block for all circle progressions

notatedExercises.title: Extended Circle (8 Measures)
notatedExercises.description: C-Am-Dm-G-Em-Am-Dm-G: A longer sequence that extends the circle pattern over two phrases.
practiceNotes: Pattern: Each chord's root is a perfect fifth below the previous
Notice how the second half mirrors the first with Em starting the sequence
Try extending this pattern even further through the full circle

notatedExercises.title: Jazz Circle with Seventh Chords
notatedExercises.description: Cmaj7-Am7-Dm7-G7-Em7-Am7-Dm7-G7: The jazz version with seventh chords for richer harmony and smoother voice leading.
practiceNotes: Voice leading: the 7th of each chord resolves down to the 3rd of the next
This creates a chain of resolutions that pulls the ear forward
Essential for jazz comping and solo guitar arrangements

notatedExercises.title: Descending Bass Line Circle
notatedExercises.description: Circle of fifths with emphasis on the descending bass movement that reinforces the harmonic direction.
practiceNotes: Bass pattern: C - A - D - G - E - A - D - G (descending by fifths)
Emphasize the bass note of each chord to hear the fifth movement
Try isolating the bass line and playing it as a single-note exercise first

sections.title: Circle of Fifths Visualization
items: Clockwise: C > G > D > A > E > B > F# > C# (ascending fifths)
Counter-clockwise: C > F > Bb > Eb > Ab > Db > Gb (ascending fourths)
Adjacent keys share the most notes in common
Keys opposite each other on the circle are maximally distant (tritone)

sections.title: Harmonic Principles
items: Movement by fifths is the strongest root motion in tonal music
Each chord shares common tones with adjacent chords in the circle
The ii-V-I progression is a segment of the circle of fifths
Full circle: C-F-Bb-Eb-Ab-Db-Gb-B-E-A-D-G-C (all 12 keys)

sections.title: Song Analysis Examples
items: "Autumn Leaves" bridge: Am7 - D7 - G / Em7 - A7 - D
"All of Me" measures 17-20: E7 - Am - Am / Dm - G7 - C
Many classical pieces use circle sequences in development sections
Pop songs often contain hidden circle of fifths fragments

sections.title: Modulation Techniques
items: Use the circle to modulate to related keys smoothly
Common-tone modulation: share notes between adjacent keys
Secondary dominants follow circle of fifths logic (V/V, V/vi, etc.)
Coltrane changes divide the circle into major third relationships
